name: Device-Related Infection (CIED / Vascular Catheter)

likely: Candida species (especially with prolonged central line dwell time, TPN)
possible: Gram-negative bacilli (less common but seen, especially with femoral lines or GI source)
pathogens.why: Device-related infections are dominated by skin-flora gram-positive organisms (coagulase-negative staphylococci, S. aureus) that colonize the device surface and form biofilm, with Candida becoming relevant in patients with prolonged central access and risk factors such as TPN or broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure.

investigations.test: Blood cultures (peripheral and through each catheter lumen if not removed)
investigations.why: Differential time-to-positivity (catheter culture positive significantly earlier than peripheral) supports a catheter-related source.
Confirms the device as the source when growth matches blood culture results.

investigations.test: Echocardiography (if S. aureus bacteremia, prosthetic valve, or persistent bacteremia)
investigations.why: Screens for endocarditis, a serious complication of device-related bacteremia, particularly with S. aureus.

investigations.test: Repeat blood cultures after line removal/initiation of therapy
investigations.why: Confirms clearance of bacteremia, especially important for S. aureus where persistent positivity changes management significantly.

references: IDSA Guidelines for Intravascular Catheter-Related Infection
AHA/ESC Infective Endocarditis Guidelines (for CIED infection)
reasonSource: e=>`Fever${e.erythemaAtSite?" with erythema/purulence at the device site":""} in a patient with an indwelling device (${[e.centralLine&&"central venous catheter",e.prostheticValve&&"prosthetic valve",e.cardiacImplantableDevice&&"cardiac implantable electronic device"].filter(Boolean).join(", ")||"indwelling device"}) raises concern for device-related infection. Source control (device removal/exchange where feasible) is as important as antibiotics — antibiotics alone frequently fail to clear infection while the device remains in place, particularly for biofilm-forming organisms.`
